content.comment_body: I have connected two [product_name] devices (one as master, one as slave) and set up output extension NQ1..NQ20 from the first unit. My client using Modbus can read outputs Q1..Q20 (addresses 8193-8212) successfully, but cannot read NQ1..NQ20 (addresses 8213-8257), as their values remain zero. The local program runs correctly, but there is an issue with Modbus communication to the client. Any suggestions? Thank you.
Could you upload your project files in a zip archive?
I hope this provides enough information.

1.) Your [product_name] is capable of Modbus TCP/IP, but you are currently using Ethernet TCP/IP with the [protocol_name] protocol instead, which is a different type of connection. 2.) Your setup uses a master/slave method, where the slave simply exposes its peripherals to the master and does not process data. Is this intentional, or was it due to lack of experience (which I suspect)? Please outline exactly what you intend to accomplish.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is working to establish communication between two [product_name] units, making one a master and the other a slave, aiming to extend outputs for access via a Modbus client. Although the main outputs are readable, the extended outputs appear inaccessible through Modbus and always return zero. Responses indicate possible confusion around communication protocols and device configuration, specifically the differences between Modbus and [protocol_name], and uncertainty about the impact of master/slave configuration. Documentation gaps and unclear protocol handling are contributing factors to user confusion.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects that linking two [product_name] devices will enable seamless access to both primary and extended outputs via a Modbus client, with straightforward support for master/slave configuration and clear mapping of extended outputs through Modbus.
pain_keywords: extended outputs not available on Modbus
